headline: Workday is turning its Sana AI assistant into the main starting screen of its HR and finance software and has agreed to buy ConductorOne, a firm that controls what AI agents may access.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a large enterprise software maker rebuilds its main interface around an AI assistant and buys an AI-agent security firm, but the claims are Workday's own and no deal terms are given.
importance_line: Staff who use Workday for hiring, leave and pay requests will deal increasingly with an AI assistant that acts for them, and companies get a way to control what their AI agents can reach, but the benefits are Workday's own claims from a product event and no deal terms or customer results are given.
summary: SiliconANGLE reports that Workday, a maker of business software for HR and finance, said at its Workday Rising conference that Sana, its agentic AI experience that gathers tasks, meetings and decisions in one place, is becoming the new Workday Home, alongside a service agent for HR and IT requests and two analysis platforms called Work Intelligence and Decision Intelligence. Workday also agreed to acquire ConductorOne, also known as C1.ai, whose platform manages which people and AI agents can reach which systems, and the report gives no price.
notes: Read in full on SiliconANGLE. Possible duplicate in category 06 (C06-13, Workday acquiring ConductorOne); this entry covers the wider Sana announcement.
